Nanopore MinIon data

Isa send me the data from Nanopore MinIon and PacBio the 28th of November. I have been uploading the data to the server, and organizing them by the species which belongs. I’m going to detail here the “notes” that Isa told me about the data, and some things that we need to consider when analize the data.

First, MinIon machine returns the sequences in fast5 format (rawdata), and then, we need to do a base calling in those files, returning the FASTQ files that we are interested in. Base calling is the process of converting the electrical signals generated by DNA or RNA strand passing through the nanopore into the corresponding base sequence of the strand. The raw data is a direct measurement of the changes in ionic current as a DNA/RNA strand passes through the pore, which are recorded by the MinKNOW software. MinIon also processes the signal into “reads”, each read corresponding to a single strand of DNA/RNA. These reads are optionally written out as .fast5 files.

We are going to perform the base calling with Guppy, a data processing toolkit that contains the Oxford Nanopore base calling algorithms and several post-processing features. The input is the raw data in .fast5 format.

In the data folder of this project, we have one folder with raw data of MinIon for two(?) individuals of Crepidostomum. Ex68_3_Crepi corresponds to two(?) pooled individuals. In that folder, we have the data in fast5 and FASTQ format. We are going to use the fast5 data for the base calling. There are 153 fast5 files. In the Phyllodistomum project we already compared the qualities of original (received) FASTQ files and those produced after our own base calling with Guppy, and we noted an improvement of the quality with our base calling. The reason may be that Guppy can be run in different modes, more or less accurate. We suspect that the original FASTQ files in ../../data/Nanopore_MinIon/Ex68_3_Crepi/fastq_pass were produced with lower accuracy, maybe on the fly, during sequencing.

Base-calling

We execute guppy_basecaller tool from Guppy for the basecalling of the rawdata.

FAST5=../../data/Nanopore_MinIon/Ex68_3_Crepi/fast5_pass
if [ ! -e CRP/sequencing_summary.txt ]; then
   guppy_basecaller -i $FAST5 -s CRP \
                    --config dna_r9.4.1_450bps_hac.cfg \
                    -q 0 --recursive --compress_fastq \
                    --num_callers 2 --cpu_threads_per_caller 16
fi

# Remove log files reporting neither errors nor success.
for file in $(ls -1 CRP/*.log); do
   if ! grep -i -e "success" -e "error" $file; then
      rm $file
   fi
done
## 2023-05-07 18:22:23.094781 [guppy/message] Basecalling completed successfully.
library(ggplot2)
summarySeq <- read.table('CRP/sequencing_summary.txt', header=TRUE)
ggplot(data = summarySeq,
       mapping = aes(x = sequence_length_template,
                     y = mean_qscore_template,
                     color = passes_filtering)) +
  geom_point() + scale_x_continuous(trans = 'log')

There are many very long reads, as well as short ones. The quality is modest.

Quality control of Nanopore data after base calling

library(fastqcr)

if (! file.exists('after_BC')) {
  fastqc(fq.dir = 'CRP', qc.dir = "after_BC",
         threads = 40, fastqc.path = "/usr/local/bin/fastqc")
}

qc.file <- list.files(path = "after_BC", all.files = FALSE,
                      full.names = TRUE, pattern = "zip")
nb_samples <- length(qc.file)

modules <- c(
  "Per sequence GC content",
  "Per base sequence quality",
  "Per sequence quality scores"
)
qc <- qc_read_collection(qc.file, sample_names = paste('S', 1:nb_samples, sep = ''),
       modules = modules)
qc_plot_collection(qc, modules = modules)
## $per_base_sequence_quality
## 
## $per_sequence_quality_scores
## 
## $per_sequence_gc_content

PacBio data

The data structure of PACBio is somewhat different from that of Nanopore. Here, the data is organized in a single 324.4Mb fastq.gz compressed file. At first, I’m not going to unzip the file for reasons of disk space, plus most of the programs I’m going to use in the pipeline accept compressed files as input.

In this case, we also have two different individuals of Crepidostomum (which are not the same as those of Nanopore!). I’m going to perform the quality analysis in the sequences fastq.gz file provided by Isa.

File name: demultiplex.bc1018_BAK8B_OA–bc1018_BAK8B_OA.hifi_reads.fastq.gz

library(fastqcr)
library(ShortRead)
PACBIO <- '../../data/PacBio/fastqs/'

if (! file.exists('report_PB')) {
  fastqc(fq.dir = PACBIO, qc.dir = "report_PB",
         threads = 40, fastqc.path = "/usr/local/bin/fastqc")
}
qc.files <- list.files(path = "report_PB", all.files = FALSE,
                       full.names = TRUE, pattern = "zip")
nb_samples <- length(qc.files)

modules <- c(
  "Per sequence GC content",
  "Per base sequence quality",
  "Per sequence quality scores"
)
qc <- qc_read_collection(qc.files, sample_names = paste('S', 1:nb_samples, sep = ''),
       modules = modules)
qc_plot_collection(qc, modules = modules)
## $per_base_sequence_quality
## 
## $per_sequence_quality_scores
## 
## $per_sequence_gc_content
fq <- '../../data/PacBio/fastqs'
pacbio <- readFastq(fq, withIds = FALSE)
barplot(table(width(pacbio)), xlab = 'Read length', ylab = 'Frequency', las = 2)

Shotgun Illumina data

Data structure

In this case, we have the data also in fastq.gz compressed format. Specifically, we have two files: 1 and 2, corresponding to the forward and reverse readings. The same as in the case of PacBio, I don’t unzip the .gz for reasons of space on the disk. It’s size is 17 Gb for the forward and 19 Gb for the reverse.

K-mer analysis

DATA="../../data/Shotgun_Illumina"

if [ ! -e reads.histo ]; then
   if [ ! -e reads.kmc_suf ]; then
      if [ ! -d kmers ]; then mkdir kmers; fi
      ls $DATA/*.fastq.gz > sg_data
      kmc -k27 -t8 @sg_data reads kmers
      #rm -r kmers
   fi
   kmc_tools transform reads histogram reads.histo
fi

if [ ! -e linear_plot.png ]; then
   if [ ! -e genomescope.R ]; then
      #wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/schatzlab/genomescope/master/genomescope.R
      wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tbenavi1/genomescope2.0/master/genomescope.R
   fi
   chmod u+x genomescope.R
   ./genomescope.R -i reads.histo -o . -k 27
fi
cat model.txt
cat summary.txt

Quality control of illumina data

Illumina <- '../../data/Shotgun_Illumina'
if (! file.exists('report_SG')) {
   fastqc(fq.dir = Illumina, qc.dir = 'report_SG',
          threads = 40, fastqc.path = '/usr/local/bin/fastqc')
}
qc.files <- list.files(path = 'report_SG', all.files = FALSE,
                       full.names = TRUE, pattern = 'zip')
nb_samples <- length(qc.files)

modules <- c('Per sequence GC content',
             'Per base sequence quality',
             'Per sequence quality scores')
qc <- qc_read_collection(qc.files, sample_names = paste('S', 1:nb_samples, sep = ''),
                         modules = modules)
qc_plot_collection(qc, modules = modules)
